Advances: ancora.derive, ancora.gate

Findings: F1 (Critical, distributed C1), F4 (High, security H1), F24 rides along (Medium, data M2). Consensus CF1 in ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
Two reproduced defects with one root cause: a git-supplied name is carried as an opaque string from the subprocess into a map key and a blob spec with no point where it becomes a validated relative path.
(a) `git diff --name-status` and `git status --porcelain` run without `-z` at lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex:56-66 and :101-114, so any path git C-quotes (non-ASCII byte, space, tab, quote, backslash) is stored as the quoted literal. Against a repo containing lib/café.ex the change set holds "lib/caf\303\251.ex"; ModuleLocator.base_sources falls through to :unchanged so base == head and no drift can ever be detected; Compare.changed_definition? filters the binding out; `mix spec.check` prints result=pass. Silent fail-open.
(b) lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:164-180 parses git cat-file --batch's "<request> missing" reply by splitting on spaces, so a request spec containing a space is read as a malformed frame. One untracked file named "my notes.txt" flips `mix spec.check` from result=pass to an unhandled RuntimeError ("gate assembly failed: {:cat_file_batch_bad_header, ...}" raised at gate.ex:466) with no verdict line. Reproduced end to end at e18fa05. Loud fail-closed with no contract.
Fix: add `-z` to both git invocations and parse NUL-delimited records (which never quote); resolve change-set paths to object ids through the existing Git.ls_tree_entries/3 and fetch by OID in prefetch/2 (change_set.ex:81), matching what BaseView already does on this branch; tag Git.read_blob/2's second argument as {:path, p} or {:oid, o} and delete the 40/64-hex regex heuristic and read_spec/2 (git.ex:14, :90-92; this is F24 and it is required because the OID fetch makes the ambiguity live); parse the missing reply from its right-hand end; add a {:cat_file_batch_bad_header, _} clause to gate_error/1 so any residual bad frame reaches the operator as tier=env with a verdict line, never a stack trace. Backstop: refuse any path that still arrives wrapped in double quotes rather than storing it.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/derive/change_set_test.exs, test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs, test/ancora/git_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate, each through a real git fixture and the real gate or CLI:
   1. An untracked file whose name contains a space: `mix spec.check` ends `spec.check result=pass` with exit 0 (today: RuntimeError, no verdict). test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:22 is the end-to-end regression proof that the reported crash is gone. Change-set prefetch now resolves base paths to object ids, so the CLI no longer sends a spaced path spec through the batch port and cannot reach the missing-reply parser. test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs:110 is the proving test for the parser mutation: restore the space-split parse and that test must fail.
  2. A changed lib/café.ex whose definition changed between base and head: the derived transition/drift finding fires (today: nothing). Mutation: drop `-z` from either git call; the test must fail.
  3. A committed file whose path contains a space, changed between base and head: prefetch resolves it by OID and the comparison sees the real base bytes. Mutation: fetch by path spec again; the test must fail.
  4. A malformed batch frame that still reaches the gate ends tier=env with a verdict line. Mutation: remove the gate_error clause; the test must fail.
  5. Git.read_blob/2 with {:path, <40 hex chars>} reads the path, not an object. Mutation: restore the regex; the test must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff (substantive, not an acknowledgment): ancora.derive (change_set_union or base_reads_batched) shall state that change-set paths are read NUL-delimited, never stored quoted, and resolved to object ids before any blob read; ancora.gate (preflight_hard_fails or the env-tier statement) shall state that a malformed cat-file frame is an environment failure with a verdict line. Decision-record edit: an affects entry or Consequences note on ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state or a new ADR; name what changed.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: the production callers are ChangeSet.compute/1 and ChangeSet.prefetch/2 reached from Gate.check/2 and Review; the proving tests are the gate/CLI fixtures above, not unit tests of the parser alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/base_view.ex (F3, ancora-kzw, and F9/F36 on ancora-d16)
- lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/mix/tasks/**
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex, lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex, lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex (only if the OID path forces a signature change)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (gate_error/1 clause and the prefetch call site only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No constraint of entry paths to the materialization root (that is ancora-kzw; do not half-fix it here). No change to BaseView's read path. No new dependency. No change to the batch-port accumulation loop (F9, deferred). Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

The module is `use Ancora.TestCase` with no async option, so it is async: true (ancora_case.exs defaults async to true). PATH is VM-global: for the ~2 s the subprocess runs, every concurrently running async module resolves `git` to the fake shim, both for run_mix_subprocess children and for in-VM Ancora.Git.run (git.ex:28 calls System.find_executable("git") at call time). Async modules that touch git during a run: spec_status_test, spec_next_test, spec_review_test, spec_validate_test, index_test, append_only_test, review_test, fresh_adopter_test.

That is already the house precedent - git_test.exs pulls the same PATH trick ("run returns data when git is absent from PATH") and is async: false. I also verified both fixes I am ordering before ordering them. The field-level assertions pass at HEAD (2 tests, 0 failures) with f.file "lib/café.ex" and "lib/my sample.ex" and f.subject "sample.subject". `use Ancora.TestCase, async: false` on spec_check_test gives 23 tests, 0 failures in 27.5s.

Bounce reason:

1. SPEC TEXT. .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md:78, the sentence "callers shall tag paths and object ids rather than infer their kind from hexadecimal text", is false in this commit. Ancora.BaseView is named in ancora.derive's own Modules block at line 22 and governed by the existing must at line 70. base_view.ex:84 passes a bare binary, and git.ex:92 keeps the untagged clause for it. base_view.ex is Out of Scope (files) and Out of Scope (intent) forbids touching BaseView's read path, so this is a text fix, not a code fix. Scope the sentence to change-set prefetch and name the BaseView exception explicitly. Do not weaken the tagging requirement where it does hold. Keep the decision record consistent in the same diff. Check that proves it: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass plus a reading of the sentence against `grep -rn "read_blob(" lib/`, which returns exactly two production callers, base_view.ex:84 bare and change_set.ex:92 tagged. Related fact for the sentence you write: after this diff no production caller passes {:path, _} at all, so blob_spec/2 survives only for a branch nothing calls.

2. TICKET RECORD plus SPEC TEXT. Behavior 1's named mutation is not killed by its named test. Reproduced above as M1. Take the honest statement, not a contrived fixture. The reason is that the fix is correct: once prefetch resolves every base path to an OID, no production path sends a spaced path spec to the port, so the space-split parse is unreachable from the CLI. A CLI fixture that reached it would have to force a path production no longer takes, which tests a dead branch and would rot the moment someone deletes it. Amend the Verification block so behavior 1 names test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs:110 as the proving test for the parser mutation, and keep test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:22 as the end-to-end regression proof that the reported crash is gone. Say in the completion record that the CLI path no longer reaches the parser and why. Check that proves it: run spec_check_test.exs:22 with the space-split parse restored and report that it passes, then run git_batch_port_test.exs and report the failure.

3. TEST ONLY, one word. test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:5 is `use Ancora.TestCase`, and ancora_case.exs:8 defaults async to true. The malformed-frame test at :34 does System.put_env("PATH", ...) for the ~2s its subprocess runs. git.ex:27 calls System.find_executable("git") at every Git.run call, so concurrent async modules resolve git to the shim in-VM as well as in subprocesses. git_test.exs already uses async: false for the same PATH trick, so the house precedent is settled. Fix: `use Ancora.TestCase, async: false`. Check that proves it: the module runs 23 tests, 0 failures (I measured 27.5s serial). The mutation it must kill is reverting to bare `use Ancora.TestCase` while any git-touching async module runs alongside it; this is a latent race, so treat the precedent and the in-VM find_executable timing as the proof, not a flake hunt.

4. TEST ONLY. test/ancora/gate_test.exs:444 and :484 assert only that "derived/drift" appears in findings_codes/1. The bug class here is a path stored under the wrong name, and Ancora.Finding carries :subject and :file, both populated at compare.ex:153. Replace both with the field-level form, following the house pattern already at gate_test.exs:655:
   assert Enum.any?(report.all_findings, fn f ->
            f.code == "derived/drift" and f.file == "lib/café.ex" and f.subject == "sample.subject"
          end)
and the same at :484 with "lib/my sample.ex". Both pass at HEAD; I ran them. Check that proves it: the M2 quoted-literal mutation must still fail both, and it does. Stating plainly that M2 is already killed by the weak assertion, so this is hardening against a fixture that later grows a second ASCII source and lets drift fire for the wrong file, not a live false pass.

5. CODE, gate.ex, in Allowed touches. The four refusals this diff introduces, {:quoted_git_path, _}, {:missing_nul_terminator, _}, {:invalid_name_status, _} and {:invalid_porcelain_status, _}, have no gate_error/1 clause and fall to the raise at gate.ex:470. Reproduced end to end as M4: empty stdout, exit 1, a RuntimeError on stderr, no verdict line. The ticket ordered the backstop that creates these refusals and ordered the cat-file clause specifically so a residual bad frame "reaches the operator as tier=env with a verdict line, never a stack trace". Give the four refusals the same treatment: gate_error/1 clauses returning {:env, run_context_error(reason)} plus run_context_error/1 messages. Check that proves it: a CLI fixture whose last stdout line equals `spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0` with no RuntimeError on stderr, in the shape of spec_check_test.exs:34. Mutation the check must kill: remove the new clauses and watch stdout go empty.

6. DOC. lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex moduledoc lines 3-5 still name the commands without -z and describe prefetch without the OID resolution step, directly above code that does both. Update it. No test; the check is reading the moduledoc against name_status/1, porcelain_status/1 and prefetch/2.

Notes (not blocking):
- Ancora.Git.run/3 defaults stderr_to_stdout: true (git.ex:26) and neither -z call opts out, while nul_records/2 now hard-requires a NUL last byte. Any git stderr noise on those two calls therefore turns into {:missing_nul_terminator, _}. I could not make real git write to stderr on `status --porcelain -z` or `diff --name-status -z`, so this is a mechanism, not a reproduced failure. Item 5 makes it survivable either way. Passing stderr_to_stdout: false on those two calls would remove the trigger, but it also drops stderr from the {:git, args, output, status} error tuple, so I am leaving that call to the implementer rather than ordering it.
- The tagged {:path, _} branch of Git.read_blob/2 has no production call site after this diff. Behavior 5 was ordered as a unit behavior so the test discharges the contract, but the standing bounce-class check about naming a production call site for each new callable surface is not met for that branch. base_view.ex is Out of Scope, so the resolution belongs to ancora-kzw, not here. Item 1's sentence should say so.
- The core fix is genuinely good. Both -z flags, the NUL parse, the OID prefetch and the malformed-frame clause each die under their named mutation and each restore green when reverted. Nothing in this bounce asks for a redesign.
- Scratch discipline held: all mutations in a detached worktree at d00f2f8 under the session scratchpad, removed with `git worktree remove --force`. The stage worktree is clean at d00f2f8.

Ran: `mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs` -> 27 tests, 0 failures, 37.0s, 0.00s async. `mix test test/ancora/gate_test.exs` -> 34 tests, 0 failures. Stage worktree clean at 41d3ff3 before and after.

=== PER-ASSERTION VERDICTS ===

ITEM 3, async: false (spec_check_test.exs:5) - PASS as ordered, but it is not an assertion.
Precedent matched: git_test.exs:5 and git_batch_port_test.exs:4 are the other two PATH mutators in the suite and both are already async: false. All three are now sync. ExUnit runs sync modules serially and after the async ones, so the race the audit named (git.ex:28 resolves the executable on every Git.run call, in-VM as well as in the subprocess) is closed. The on_exit PATH restore is safe across the process boundary because System.put_env writes VM-global state, not process state.
No test goes red if this word is removed. See the record section below.

ITEM 4, field-level drift (gate_test.exs:443-447 and :487-491) - PASS.
Exactly the form the audit dictated, matching the house pattern at gate_test.exs:663. `finding.file` and `finding.subject` are compared by equality inside an existence predicate over report.all_findings, which is the right shape: the old `"derived/drift" in findings_codes(...)` passed if drift fired for any file under any subject.
Honest caveat: the subject half is close to vacuous here, since sample.subject is the only subject in both fixtures. The file half is the load-bearing one, and it is the half M2 (store the C-quoted literal) kills. Both files carry a real non-ASCII byte and a real 0x20, per the earlier fixture-honesty check.

ITEM 5, the four CLI refusal fixtures (spec_check_test.exs:71-120) - PASS.
How they provoke each refusal: a /bin/sh script named `git` written to <root>/fake-bin and prepended to PATH, dispatching on `$3`. Ancora.Git.run/3 builds argv as ["-C", root | args] at git.ex:34, so $3 is always the subcommand. Every other subcommand hits `exec "$real_git" "$@"`, and real_git is captured with System.find_executable before PATH is touched. Same shim shape as the pre-existing malformed-frame test at :34, which the prior audit already cleared on honesty. The new ones additionally quote "$real_git".
Free of production calls: yes. No production module is named in any of the four tests. The four expected operator strings are hardcoded literals, not produced by calling run_context_error/1, and the malformed bytes come from shell printf, not from ChangeSet.
Each fixture reaches a distinct clause. Traced by reading against lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex:
- `M\0"lib/sample.ex"\0` -> nul_records ok -> name_status_entries [code, path] -> validate_path/1 sees the leading and trailing quote -> {:quoted_git_path, _}.
- `M\0lib/sample.ex` -> :binary.last is not 0 -> {:missing_nul_terminator, :name_status}.
- `M\0` -> one record -> past both name_status_entries clauses -> {:invalid_name_status, ["M"]}.
- `invalid\0` on the status call -> byte 3 is not a space, so no porcelain clause matches -> {:invalid_porcelain_status, ["invalid"]}. For this one `git diff` stays real and returns empty against the clean fixture tree, so name_status returns {:ok, []} first and the porcelain error is genuinely the one that fires.
Four tuples, four distinct run_context_error/1 clauses. No two fixtures prove the same clause.
Assertions, all four: `result.status == 1`; `result.stdout =~ <message>` with a distinct message per case; `List.last(lines(result.stdout)) == "spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0"` by equality, and lines/1 splits with trim: true so that really is the last non-empty stdout line; `refute result.stderr =~ "RuntimeError"`.
The verdict-line equality is what carries the check. `status == 1` alone does not discriminate, because an uncaught raise also exits 1. Neither lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex nor lib/ancora/gate.ex has a rescue, so deleting a gate_error/1 clause gives an uncaught RuntimeError with empty stdout and a stderr banner, which is the M4 shape the audit reproduced. Three of the four assertions name that.

=== FINDINGS (none blocking) ===

1. Uncovered message clause. `run_context_error({:missing_nul_terminator, :porcelain_status})` at gate.ex:512 has no fixture; only the :name_status sibling does. Deleting it falls to the catch-all "cannot start git read context: ...", which still returns tier=env with a verdict line, so this degrades the operator message rather than restoring the crash. The audit ordered four fixtures and got four. Naming it so nobody is surprised later.

2. Narrow stack-trace refutation. `refute stderr =~ "RuntimeError"` names one exception module. An ErlangError, MatchError or ArgumentError banner slips past it. `refute result.stderr =~ "** ("` would catch any Elixir exception banner. This is pre-existing house style (identical line at :29 and :69), so it is a suggestion for the file, not a defect of this diff.

3. Dead tag. `@tag change_set_refusal: true` at :84 is the only occurrence in the repo, and test_helper.exs is a bare ExUnit.start() with no include/exclude. It selects nothing. Harmless, but it reads like a filter that exists.

4. Weakening relative to d00f2f8: NONE. The only deleted test lines are the two `assert "derived/drift" in findings_codes(...)` lines, each replaced by a strictly stronger assertion, plus the module header line. No test removed, no assertion loosened, no fixture shrunk.

=== THE RECORD DOES NOT MATCH THE TREE (read this before verifying) ===

The IMPLEMENTED record claims six mutation proofs. Three of them name assertions that do not exist anywhere in the tree:
- item 1: "the caller/spec semantic assertion failed 1, then passed 1"
- item 6: "the code-to-doc assertion failed 1, then passed 1"
- item 3: "removed async: false; the isolation assertion failed 1"
The diff adds no test for items 1, 3 or 6. The worktree is clean at 41d3ff3. Nothing under test/ reads .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, nothing calls Code.fetch_docs on Ancora.Derive.ChangeSet, and nothing asserts a module's async flag.

The work itself is correct, because the audit ordered no test for any of the three. Item 1's check is reading the sentence against `grep -rn "read_blob(" lib/`. Item 6 says in as many words "No test; the check is reading the moduledoc". Item 3 says to treat the precedent and the in-VM find_executable timing as the proof, "not a flake hunt". So the defect is the record, not the suite: three prose checks were written up in the grammar of failing-then-passing ExUnit assertions.

Answering the question directly: they are not text-pinning tests, because they are not tests, and they pin nothing. That is the right outcome. Had they been written as text-pinning tests (the repo has the pattern in eight files via Code.fetch_docs), the moduledoc one would break on a harmless rewording and the spec-sentence one on any reflow, which is presumably why the audit ordered reading checks instead. I would leave it that way.
Ask of the verifier: do not go hunting for those three assertions, and do not accept "failed 1, then passed 1" as evidence for items 1, 3 or 6. Confirm those three by reading, as the audit specified.

=== MUTATIONS FOR THE VERIFIER ===
Reading cannot establish that an assertion goes red, only what it names. Each of these is a named mutation, not an observed failure.
- M-a: delete the four gate_error/1 clauses at gate.ex:470-485. Run `mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs`. Expect 4 failures, each with empty stdout and a RuntimeError banner on stderr.
- M-b: delete only `run_context_error({:quoted_git_path, path})` at gate.ex:503, leaving its gate_error/1 clause. Expect exactly 1 failure, on the stdout message substring, with the verdict line still correct. This is what proves the four message clauses are individually pinned rather than jointly.
- M-c: make validate_path/1 in change_set.ex always return :ok. Expect 1 failure in spec_check_test (quoted Git path) alongside the 2 gate_test drift failures the audit already measured as M2.
- M-d: revert spec_check_test.exs:5 to bare `use Ancora.TestCase`. UNVERIFIED BY READING and not verifiable by running either: no assertion goes red, by design. The proof is the git_test.exs precedent and the per-call System.find_executable at git.ex:28. I checked both.
